items.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So when he was eighteen I took him with me for a while.

ctx.x: I‘m trying to think. Okay, Stump was trying to do a little work, but he couldn‘t. He lost the use of his right hand. He had trouble holding his sticks. And then I‘m trying to think; there was somebody in there. Nobody I really loved, you know. It was just a

drummer here. Oh, oh, oh, okay. Who came through there was Warren Shad, when he was a little boy. I knew his family. I knew his dad since I was about fifteen, sixteen years old. And I said, ―When you grow up, you‘re going to play in my band. Okay?‖ So when he was eighteen I took him with me for a while. He‘s good. He‘s quite a musician. Warren, that‘s just about it. Yeah, because Warren was with me just to do rehearsals every week. I was playing at the One Step Down. We played all Sunday night. [unclear] tired of…
